summary: Short renewal/expansion check-in. Equinox asking for committed capacity increase for Q4 usage forecast and wanting EU region + clarity on egress billing. Rediscussed dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, private VPC path and security docs. Action: pricing SOW and perf benchmark + legal review scheduling.
transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-07-19 Time: 16:00 UTC Duration: ~52m Attendees: Evelyn Ward (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Olivia Chen (Redwood CSM), Lena Torres (CTO, Equinox), Marcus Hu (Head of ML), Priya Rao (Procurement), Tom Gallagher (Infra)
[00:00] Evelyn: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep this to about 45, 50 minutes — wanted to go through capacity ask, EU onboarding and egress concerns.
[00:14] Lena: Yeah thanks, quick context — we've been seeing uptick in traffic, forecast looks like 2.3x by November with new feature. We want to lock a committed capacity uplift and get EU region live for latency/residency.
[00:28] Samir: Cool, can you give a bit more on token distribution and p95 latency targets? that helps sizing.
[00:33] Marcus: Most of our traffic is chat-style, average 400 tokens per session, p95 latency target ~450ms for interactive flows; peak concurrency about 1,200 concurrent sessions, sustained throughput around 150k tokens/minute.
[00:52] Evelyn: Okay that aligns with a 3-4 instance equivalent on dedicated for our M40-type offering — or on hosted we can do a reserved burst plan but costs dif — sorry, cost delta.
[01:05] Tom: On the infra side we prefer VPC peering, we need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM and KMS integration for key rotation. Are those supported in the private path?
[01:16] Olivia: Yes, the Redwood Pryvate option supports customer KMS and audit streaming; note: sometimes the transcribed docs call it Redwood Privatee in older notes. We'll share SOC2 and the KMS integration runbook.
[01:29] Priya: For procurement I need to understand the billing model for egress — in EU our egress charges are sensitive, how does Redwood bill cross-region egress when we route to eu-west-1?
[01:41] Evelyn: Short answer: hosted plan shows outbound egress line item (per-GB) plus per-token. On Dedicated with geo pinning, egress is typically lower because inference stays in region but cross-region failover can incur egress. We'll put numbers in the worksheet.
[01:56] Marcus: Also, model variants — we currently run a quantized 7B for most flows, but will need to test LLM-13 for some higher quality routes. Any guidance on throughput per variant?
[02:09] Samir: We'll run benchmarks for both variants; the 13B will need higher memory and will reduce batch size for same latency SLO. We'll propose a split: 70% 7B, 30% 13B for costing and capacity configuration.
[02:23] Lena: Security wise, SOC2 plus more granular RBAC is a must — we also need audit trail retention of one year. Is that configurable?
[02:31] Olivia: Yes retention windows are configurable on the Console; for Private deployments retention can be customer-controlled. We'll send the retention matrix.
[02:43] Priya: Legal: we have a tight renewal window — we need contract extension by end of July to avoid price resets. Can you accommodate that timeline?
[02:52] Evelyn: Yes, if we get confirmation on committed uplift and region selection this week, we'll route a SOW amendment + pricing and legal can review by Jul 29.
[03:04] Tom: How about performance fallbacks — if eu region is overloaded do you failover to us-east-1? will that trigger egress and higher latencies we need to account for?
[03:13] Samir: Routing policy is config'able — can set strict region-only, or soft-failover with autoscaling. Failover will cause cross-region egress and latency increases. We'll include failover latency profiles in the benchmark doc.
[03:28] Marcus: Any mention of competitors — we ran a quick POC with Bedrock earlier, found their cold-start times were worse but egress pricing was similar. We're weighing total cost, not just token price.
[03:41] Evelyn: Understood — we'll surface per-token, per-GB egress, and expected p95 in the pricing sheet so you can compare apples-to-apples.
[03:52] Priya: On procurement items, we need an amendment that calls out minimum commitment, price tiers, and an exit clause for non-performance.
[04:02] Evelyn: We'll propose a 12-month amendment with a mid-year review and SLA credits aligned to p99 availability.
[04:12] Lena: For EU region selection, we're leaning towards eu-central-1 due to vendor footprint, but want your latency numbers.
[04:21] Samir: We'll run region-specific benchmarks from your test agents and share. We suggest KV cache priming for interactive flows to reduce p95.
[04:30] Marcus: What's the expected time to provision EU dedicated capacity once SOW signed?
[04:36] Evelyn: Typical lead time 4–6 weeks for dedicated geocluster, 1–2 weeks for hosted region activation. We'll include exact timelines in the SOW.
[04:48] Tom: Ops question: can we bring our own GPU nodes for private? we have on-prem infra we'd like to reuse.
[04:55] Samir: There's an on-prem integration path but it requires our infra team to run the runtime packaging; it's treated like a Redwood Private on-prem install. We'll send the integration checklist; note there are some kernel/driver quirks.
[05:08] Lena: Ok great. I think we have enough to move forward — would like the SOW and pricing by the 22nd.
[05:15] Evelyn: We'll do that. quick recap: Redwood sends pricing + SOW amendment, Samir runs perf benchmarks for both model variants and with KV cache, Lena confirms EU region preference, Priya schedules legal review. Anything else?
[05:29] Priya: Please include sample amendment language for egress caps and SLA credits.
[05:35] Olivia: We'll attach SOC2 and KMS runbook to the follow-up email.
[05:40] Marcus: Also include an ops playbook for failover scenarios.
[05:45] Evelyn: Noted. Thanks all, we'll follow up with the packet and book the legal call. End of call.
